subject: Marketplace listing exception & integration asks — CloudBridge SI package
messages:
From: Helena Park <helena@cloudbridge.co>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace <marketplace-listings@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: exception for CloudBridge SI package listing on AWS Marketplace

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudBridge is excited about the Redwood runtime. We're working on a co-listed offering (CloudBridge-managed SI + Redwood inference) and the Marketplace team asked us to request an exception because our package bundles a private-dedicated deployment + managed onboarding (non-standard SKU mapping).

Quick summary of asks from our side:
- We need Redwood to support a custom product listing that maps a single Marketplace SKU to a provisioning flow that spins up a dedicated pool and includes a managed onboarding work item.
- We also need an expected SLA and estimated lead time for provisioning (we're targeting 2–4 business days).
- The marketplace team requested a security addendum and a short integration spec we can attach to the listing.

I've attached our package overview (cloudbridge_package_overview.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support an exception path and what product changes (if any) are required?

Helena
Head of Partnerships | CloudBridge

Attachments:
- cloudbridge_package_overview.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Helena Park <helena@cloudbridge.co>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: exception for CloudBridge SI package listing on AWS Marketplace

Hi Helena —

Appreciate the detail and the overview. We're interested in supporting this, but need to validate a few things before we commit to the Marketplace exception:

1) Provisioning automation: is the dedicated pool created per-customer or per-SKU? We need the exact desired mapping so we can align our provisioning templates.
2) Billing mapping: does CloudBridge expect Redwood to invoice usage, or will CloudBridge handle billing and expect a passthrough license model?
3) Security artifacts: please send the marketplace checklist items you require. We can provide SOC2 evidence and a signed security addendum, but may need 48–72 hours for internal sign-off.

Internal cc: Marcus, Ava — can you two take a look at the attached overview and flag technical gaps for a custom SKU->provisioning flow? If it's feasible, we should scope the minimal runtime and console changes, estimate lead time, and list any follow-on product work (e.g., SKU mapping UI, billing integration).

Helena — assuming we can meet the security request and provisioning pattern, would CloudBridge accept a phased launch (Marketplace listing points to a partner-managed onboarding link for 30 days, then move to direct turnkey provisioning)?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

--
Priya Natarajan
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: CloudBridge marketplace exception — product asks & owners

Team —

CloudBridge has asked for a non-standard Marketplace SKU that maps to a provisioning flow which:
- Creates a dedicated GPU pool (reserved) per customer
- Triggers a managed onboarding ticket (partner-run) that includes custom prompt/role setup
- Requires us to attach security/integration documentation to the listing

Questions / items to scope:
- Marcus: can our provisioning API accept a single SKU signal to trigger a dedicated_pool.create(customer_id, pool_config)? What surface changes are needed in the console and control plane?
- Ava: what UI/ops changes would we need to expose a SKU mapping page in the Console? Minimal approach: an admin mapping table + webhook to CloudBridge onboarding form.
- Rafael: billing — can we support partner-managed billing (CloudBridge invoices customers) or do we require usage to flow through Redwood (if so, what changes needed to map SKU->billing record)?
- Grace: security/compliance — we will need a quick turn on the security addendum. What's the minimum artifact set CloudBridge needs for the listing?

Desired timeline: If feasible, aim for a phased go-live within 3 weeks (provisioning proof-of-concept in 7–10 days). This is aggressive; please call out blockers and risk.

I'll coordinate a short working session tomorrow to align owners.

Thanks,
Priya
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudBridge marketplace exception — product asks & owners

Priya / team —

Quick feasibility notes after an initial pass:
- Provisioning: technically doable. We already have an API that creates reserved pools; mapping a single SKU to a provisioning playbook is a configuration-layer change (no runtime kernel changes).
- Console: minimal Console change required — admin-only SKU mapping table + a webhook that calls the existing provisioning API. Rough estimate: 3 dev sprints (2 backend, 1 frontend) if we staff it as a priority.
- Billing: supporting partner-managed billing without routing usage through Redwood is possible but means we cannot provide per-customer token-level billing in our Console. If CloudBridge wants Redwood to surface usage numbers, we'll need a billing ingest endpoint (adds ~1 sprint).
- Security: no blockers — the standard SOC2 package + a one-page addendum should satisfy marketplace team. I'll attach a short integration spec with endpoints we'll need.

Attachments:
- marketplace_integration_spec.md (Markdown, 12KB)

Risk callouts:
- SLA: provisioning ETA of 2–4 business days is achievable but requires provisioning webhook reliability and some automation around capacity allocation.
- Rollout: prefer phased launch behind a partner-managed onboarding link for the first 30 days to reduce immediate console/UX risk.

Happy to sync with CloudBridge in the working session.

— Marcus
Senior Product Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Helena Park <helena@cloudbridge.co>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: exception for CloudBridge SI package listing on AWS Marketplace

Hi Helena —

Thanks for the package overview. After an internal review, we can support the Marketplace exception with a phased approach. High-level plan:

Phase 1 (partner-managed onboarding):
- Marketplace SKU routes customers to CloudBridge-managed onboarding link. CloudBridge provisions the Redwood dedicated pool via an authenticated webhook to our provisioning API.
- Redwood provides SOC2 artifacts and signs the marketplace security addendum.
- Target: provisioning POC in 7–10 business days; listing with partner-managed onboarding in ~2 weeks.

Phase 2 (optional direct provisioning):
- Redwood implements an admin SKU->provisioning mapping in the Console and a billing ingest endpoint if you want usage surfaced in our Console. Estimated 3 dev sprints.

Action items for CloudBridge:
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to surface usage in our Console (this affects billing work).
- Please sign the attached security addendum (we've prepared a one-page addendum to attach to the Marketplace listing). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/placeholder-security-addendum
- Share the Marketplace checklist items the AWS team requires so we can attach the right artifacts.

Attachments:
- security_addendum_signed.pdf (PDF, 8KB) — draft for signature

If that sounds OK, let's schedule a 30-minute working session Monday to align the provisioning webhook contract and go/no-go for the phased timeline.

Best,
Priya
From: Helena Park <helena@cloudbridge.co>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace <marketplace-listings@amazon.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: exception for CloudBridge SI package listing on AWS Marketplace

Hi Priya (and team) —

This plan works for us. Quick confirms:
- CloudBridge will handle initial billing and invoice customers directly for the first 30 days (so we do not need Redwood to ingest billing during Phase 1).
- We'll sign the security addendum and return it via DocuSign by EOD Monday.
- Go-live target for Phase 1: Nov 30th — that gives us two weeks to validate provisioning and update the Marketplace listing copy.

We'll be ready for the Monday working session. Marcus — thanks for the spec; we'll review and send any edge-case provisioning requirements.

Best —
Helena
